citations.review_text: I wanted to come back to this game as I remember it being pretty good come to learn it has 500 concurrent players and is being shut down in less than 6 months If companies can terminate a game at anytime, then I should be allowed a refund at anytime.

I bought New World with the hope that it would grow into the MMO it was marketed to be. Instead, it struggled from the start — technical issues, unstable multiplayer, and design changes that never really fixed the core problems. I stepped away for a long time and came back hoping to finally enjoy what I paid for, only to find out the game is being shut down entirely

It’s frustrating to see a full‑price MMO end like this, especially when many players barely got the experience they were promised. I can’t recommend this game to anyone, and I wish the situation had been handled with more respect for the community that supported it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features good graphics, sound design, and an immersive atmosphere.

citations.review_text:
New World: Aeternum is a game that sits in a very complicated place in the MMORPG landscape. Objectively looking at the history and the current state of the game, it is a classic example of a title with immense potential that has struggled significantly with execution and player retention.

Here is an honest breakdown of the current consensus:

The core combat system is arguably the game’s greatest strength. Unlike many traditional MMOs that rely on "tab-targeting," New World features a real-time, action-oriented combat system that feels responsive, weighty, and skill-based. When you swing a great axe or dodge an incoming arrow, it feels satisfying in a way that very few other MMOs manage to replicate. The world of Aeternum itself is also visually stunning, with top-tier sound design and an atmospheric, supernatural island aesthetic that makes initial exploration genuinely captivating.

However, the "Mixed" overall rating and "Mostly Negative" recent reviews reflect deep-seated issues that the community has been vocal about for years. The content cycle has historically been slow, leading to long periods of stagnation where players felt there was nothing left to do. Even with the "Aeternum" relaunch/rebranding efforts, many long-term players feel that fundamental problems—such as endgame variety, balance issues, and technical bugs—have not been fully addressed.

A major point of contention often cited by the community is the "endgame loop." While the leveling process and the initial journey through Aeternum are fun, the endgame can quickly turn into an repetitive grind. Additionally, while the game is an open-world MMORPG, the economy and the influence of powerful factions can sometimes make the world feel restrictive rather than open, especially for solo players or those not deeply embedded in a top-tier company.

The verdict is that New World is a beautiful, ambitious game that hits the "fun" mark perfectly for the first 50 to 100 hours. If you want an action-packe…

A Farewell to Aeternum

I poured more than 70 hours into New World when it launched, and I loved every minute of it. I stepped away for a while, life doing what life does, and when I finally returned… I was met with the news that the game will be shutting down on January 31, 2027. That one stings.

It’s hard not to feel disappointed. Six million copies sold in the first month alone — over $200 million in revenue — and that’s just Steam. With numbers like that, you’d think this world would have had a longer life. But here we are, watching another ambitious MMO fade out far sooner than it deserved.

So now I’ve got six months to return, to catch up, and to enjoy this beautiful, flawed, unforgettable work of art one last time. Because despite everything, New World was something special. The atmosphere, the sound design, the weight of every swing, the forests that felt alive — Aeternum was a place worth getting lost in.

To the Island of Aeternum: thank you. For the adventures, the chaos, the beauty, the grind, the friendships, and the memories. If this truly is the sunset, I hope it’s a breathtaking one.
Good graphics, good audio, good combat, good crafting. Overall fun to play. Yet to get to end game. Will update my comment if I do.

A Slap in the Face to the Community. I loved the world, the combat, and the grind of New World: Aeternum. Knowing that everything I achieved, every hour I put in, and every dollar I spent is entirely erased because Amazon decided it wasn't profitable enough is incredibly disheartening. 
Zero Player Refunds: Amazon is walking away with our cash, refusing to offer refunds for a premium product they are actively breaking. Wasted Progression: Years of hard work, grinding, and building up characters are completely gone with zero offline fallback options. 
Amazon Boycott: This is a harsh reminder of modern gaming corporate greed. Because of this absolute disrespect to our time and wallets, I will no longer be purchasing Amazon Games titles or any other Amazon products. They didn't even bother to leave it in an indefinite maintenance mode—they are completely pulling the plug.
Avoid this company at all costs.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as featuring physics-backed, directional, and non-tab-targeting mechanics where each weapon relies on three active skills supported by passives.

citations.review_text:
This is not a review. This is a tribute to a one-of-a-kind game that fell into the wrong hands. Even with all its flaws, being far from perfect, it delivered an unmatched, grounded experience:
Organic Combat - A physics-backed, directional system free from tab-targeting. Every dodge, block, and strike required true aiming and positioning, giving weapons a satisfying sense of weight and skill.
Living World Interaction - An immersive sandbox driven by arguably the best audio and gathering design in MMO history. The echo of a pickaxe against ore and the physical crash of falling timber made the world feel tangible and alive.
Realistic Graphic Design - A breathtaking, gritty, historical-fantasy aesthetic.
This game deserves better.

New World.  A Love-Hate Relationship After Nearly 2,000 Hours

Where do I begin with New World?

For me, New World has always been a love-hate relationship. There are aspects of the game that I genuinely love, and they're some of the best features I've experienced in an MMO. At the same time, there are design decisions that stop it from reaching its full potential.

Let's start with the positives.

The combat is one of New World's greatest strengths. Its simplicity is refreshing. Instead of overwhelming players with dozens of abilities, each weapon focuses on just three active skills supported by passive talents. That makes combat easy to understand while still allowing room for skill and different playstyles.

The mounts are another fantastic addition. They feel responsive, improve exploration, and make travelling across Aeternum much more enjoyable.

Unfortunately, this is where my biggest criticism begins.

The game's endgame is heavily centred around PvP. Whether it's Outpost Rush, Arenas, Wars, the PvP reward track, or open-world PvP, almost every meaningful progression system encourages or outright requires player-versus-player content. Even activities like Invasions, while technically PvE, are designed in a way that feels heavily influenced by the game's PvP focus.

As someone who enjoys PvE just as much as PvP, I think this is where New World loses its balance.

The PvE experience quickly becomes repetitive. Most quests follow the same basic formula: travel somewhere, defeat a few enemies, interact with an object or NPC, then return to hand the quest in. There is very little variety.

I'd have loved to see more quests involving crafting, gathering, exploration, puzzles, or multi-stage objectives that rewarded players for engaging with every part of the game rather than simply running between quest markers.

The player-driven economy is another issue.
